batchPipeline.title: Data Lakehouse Pipeline: Cloud-Ready Data Engineering
batchPipeline.description: An e-commerce analytics pipeline that extracts data from a public API, preserves the raw layer, cleans and standardizes the data, and publishes analytical aggregations. The MVP runs locally with Docker, Airflow and PostgreSQL and is designed to evolve toward managed cloud services.
batchPipeline.imageAlt: Data pipeline architecture diagram with Bronze, Silver and Gold layers

caseStudy.label: Problem
caseStudy.text: Demonstrate a complete batch flow for ingesting, transforming and serving e-commerce analytics data from a public API.

caseStudy.label: Context
caseStudy.text: Originally developed as a technical challenge and adapted for this portfolio. The MVP runs locally; the cloud architecture described in the repository is a reference evolution, not a verified execution.

caseStudy.label: Architecture
caseStudy.text: The API feeds the Bronze layer, data is treated in Silver and aggregated in Gold, and the result is loaded into PostgreSQL. Apache Airflow can orchestrate the stages through the pipeline_ecommerce_medallion DAG.

caseStudy.label: Solution
caseStudy.text: Python extraction, raw-data preservation, typing and standardization with Parquet conversion, analytical modeling and final loading for BI consumption.

caseStudy.label: Technologies
caseStudy.text: Python, pandas, Apache Airflow, Docker, PostgreSQL and Parquet. The README also documents future options with S3, Kinesis, Glue, Spark, Iceberg and Lambda, without claiming they are implemented in the MVP.

caseStudy.label: My contribution
caseStudy.text: I implemented the batch pipeline and adapted the technical challenge into a data-focused portfolio project. I also structured a cloud-ready evolution from the original on-premise processing to an AWS-oriented architecture, keeping the boundary between local execution and production reference explicit.

caseStudy.label: Technical challenges
caseStudy.text: The main challenge was designing a scalable evolution for data originally processed on-premise: separating ingestion, treatment and consumption into Bronze, Silver and Gold layers, orchestrating the stages with Airflow and simulating the move to AWS services without presenting the simulation as a real deployment.

caseStudy.label: Result
caseStudy.text: A functional end-to-end batch flow with preserved raw data, Parquet transformations, analytical aggregations and Gold-layer loading into PostgreSQL. The repository also documents the cloud-ready evolution and includes visual evidence of the pipeline layers; no volume, runtime or quality metrics were published.

caseStudy.label: GitHub / demonstration
caseStudy.text: GitHub contains the code, README, architecture diagram and Bronze, Silver and Gold visual evidence. The video demonstration mentioned in the README is currently unavailable.
